sn55.54:5.7: Compare Sāriputta’s teaching to Dhanañjāni at [mn97:30.1]().
sn55.54:7.12: In the Dhanañjānisutta, Sāriputta only taught as far as the Brahmā realm, for which the Buddha chastised him.
sn55.54:8.3: This passage shows that a lay person can attain arahantship, at least on their deathbed. At [pli-tv-kd1:7.11.1](), the layman Yasa attains arahantship and immediately ordains. From these cases, the later tradition asserted that if a lay person becomes an arahant, they *must* either ordain or die that very day ([mil6.2.2]()). But this oversteps the Suttas. While an arahant must live a celibate life of detachment, which ordination is supposed to support, nothing in the Suttas precludes other means of achieving the same end. | See note on deathbed conversions at [sn55.21:1.13]().
